we have designed, synthesized, and characterized a nebramine-conjugated cyclam molecule that is able show synergy with existing antibiotics, including β-lactam and β-lactam inhibitor combinations, to treat multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas strains.

we have designed a new class of antibacterial adjuvants that can potentiate existing antibiotics, including β-lactam-β-lactam inhibitor combinations, against multidrug resistant and extremely drug-resistant P. aerugenosa strains in vitro.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antibiotics and adjuvants that will help to address the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance.
the discovery and development of novel antibacterial compounds to address the increasing problem of multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, specifically P. aeruginos.
the development of a new antibacterial adjuvants that is able to enhance the activity of existing antibiotics against multidrug- resistant P. aeruginosis strains.

the nebramine cyclam conjugate is a potentiated β-lactam antibiotic against multidrug resistant P. aeruginos.
the nebramine cyclam conjugate is an effective adjuvant for β-lactams against multidrug-resistant phenotypic P. aeruginosae.

the nebramine conjugate is an effective adjuvant that can potentiate existing β-Lactams against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, and that this adjuvants’ mechanism of action is likely to be through outer membrane permeabilisation.

the nebramine conjugate can be used in combination with β-lactam and other antibiotic classes against P. aerugenosa strains that are multidrug-resistant and/or β-lactam-resistant.

we have developed a nebramine conjugate that can enhance the efficacy of β-lactams and other legacy antibiotics against multidrug- and extremely drug-resistant P. aerugionsa in vitro, and we have also identified a mechanism of action for this adjuvant.
